content.user_title: Add Camera Capture to React Apps
content.value_statement: Web camera integration requires permission handling, preview state, and device controls. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through the provided React hook.
actual_capabilities: Integrates the @caffeineai/camera useCamera hook into React components.
Configures camera direction, ideal dimensions, image quality, and image format.
Connects video and canvas references for previews and photo capture.
Adds controls for starting, stopping, switching, retrying, and capturing.
Handles browser support, loading state, and camera errors.
limitations: Requires browser camera support and user permission.
Does not define photo upload, storage, or image processing workflows.
The documented type declaration and usage example contain inconsistencies that require package verification.

use_cases.title: Build a Camera Form
use_cases.description: Add a responsive preview and photo capture controls to a React form.

use_cases.title: Create Mobile Capture
use_cases.description: Implement rear-camera capture and supported camera switching for a mobile workflow.

use_cases.title: Cover Camera States
use_cases.description: Add loading, permission, unsupported-browser, and retry states to a camera interface.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Preview
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a React camera preview using @caffeineai/camera. Include start and stop controls, responsive dimensions, and visible permission errors.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Photo
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a camera component that previews video and captures a photo. Disable actions until initialization completes and handle a failed capture.

prompt_templates.title: Support Mobile Cameras
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a mobile camera interface with front and rear modes. Enable switching only when supported and preserve stable preview dimensions.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Camera State Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this camera component: [component]. Correct permission, timeout, loading, retry, cleanup, and desktop switching behavior using the documented hook.

output_examples.input: Add a basic camera preview to a React form.
output: A responsive preview connected to the hook video reference.
Start and stop controls that follow loading and active states.
Visible messages for permission and support errors.

output_examples.input: Design a mobile photo capture workflow.
output: A rear-camera default for document or product capture.
A capture action available only while the camera is active.
Camera switching shown only on supported devices.

output_examples.output: The review identifies missing permission feedback, premature controls, collapsed preview dimensions, retry gaps, and unsupported desktop switching.

best_practices: Disable camera actions while initialization or switching is in progress.
Give the preview explicit dimensions and a stable responsive aspect ratio.
Explain camera use clearly and rely on browser permission controls before capture.
anti_patterns: Do not start the camera on pages where users do not expect capture.
Do not hide permission, support, timeout, or device errors.
Do not assume camera switching works on every desktop or mobile device.

faq.question: Which framework does this skill support?
faq.answer: It documents a React hook supplied by the @caffeineai/camera package.

faq.question: Does camera access require permission?
faq.answer: Yes. The browser controls camera permission, and the interface should display permission errors.

faq.question: Can users switch cameras?
faq.answer: The hook exposes switching, but applications should enable it only on supported devices.

faq.question: Which image formats are available?
faq.answer: The documented configuration lists JPEG, PNG, and WebP.

faq.question: Does the skill upload captured photos?
faq.answer: No. It covers local capture through the hook, not upload or storage.

faq.question: How should unsupported browsers be handled?
faq.answer: Check the support state, avoid enabling camera actions, and show a clear message.
